# AudioDecoderOptions

[DotGame.AudioCodecs](README.md) · `DotGame.AudioCodecs` · class

```csharp
public sealed class AudioDecoderOptions
```

The settings of a [`FlacDecoder`](FlacDecoder.md) or [`OpusDecoder`](OpusDecoder.md) (WAV has none).

## Properties

### SkipChecksums

```csharp
public bool SkipChecksums { get; init; }
```

Whether the checksums over the audio go unchecked as a file is read: each Ogg page's CRC and each FLAC frame's CRC-16. The default, `false`, checks them, so damage to the audio is an `IO.InvalidDataException`. Skipping them saves their time, at the cost of decoding damage the format still parses as noise instead, perhaps differently from memory, from a stream and after a seek.

The checks are cheap where the processor multiplies without carries (PCLMULQDQ on x64, PMULL on Arm64): under 1% of a decode, on a 2019 phone too. Elsewhere (WebAssembly) they're table lookups, a few percent of a FLAC decode and about 1% of an Opus one.

The checks that find where a page or frame starts are kept: a FLAC frame header's CRC-8, and the CRC of an Ogg page found by a seek or at the file's end.
